text.p: These are the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Countdown starts to direct talks with the Turkish Cypriot side in New York. President Glafcos Clerides says he is prepared to sign a new concise high-level agreement with the Turkish side which is not open to misinterpretations.
- Hot air masses from Libya brought on a heatwave with temperatures nudging 42 degrees.
- Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash arrive in New York for the U.N. sponsored direct talks, but both appear to be in an uncompromising mood.
- The Central Bank of Cyprus defends its record on the fight against money laundering.
- Customs officials are involved in the flesh trade. Communist Akel deputy Kikis Yiangou claims customs officials have been spotted picking up foreign cabaret entertainers from airports.
- New Turkish threats for the qualitative and quantative upgrading of the Turkish occupying forces in Cyprus overshadow the New York talks.
- The direct talks start in New York tomorrow with a 10 point plan submitted by former British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind during his visit to Cyprus in December.
